title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting Using Chronos-2 Foundation Model
note: Fetched. Data: Jul 2023 to Jan 2025; test 8 Jul 2024 to 15 Jan 2025, 192 days, 177 scored after 15 fully missing days. 10.6% of hours imputed from day-type templates; imputed hours are not scored but stay in contexts (46% of 28-day contexts hold one or more). Metrics are daily CV-RMSE and MAPE, averaged over days.

title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting Using Chronos-2 Foundation Model
note: Fetched. Headline, 28-day context: CV-RMSE 14.58% with no covariates against 10.41% with day type as past and future covariate; MAPE 9.33% against 6.75%. With 7 days the no-covariate figure is 18.73% CV-RMSE, 11.17% MAPE. Past-only covariates give no systematic gain. Reference methods: weekly seasonal naive 31.75% / 22.24%, day-type median template 19.25% / 12.57%.

title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting Using Chronos-2 Foundation Model
note: Fetched. Weather: past plus future weather alone is about equal to or slightly worse than no covariates; weather plus day type beats no covariates but not day type alone (Holm-corrected p at least 0.32 on changeover days; day type alone slightly better on stable days, significant only at 14 days). Swapping archived forecasts for observed weather changes nothing significant (177 paired days).

title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting Using Chronos-2 Foundation Model
note: Fetched. Where the gain sits: on days whose type differs from the day before; on stable days no difference (p above 0.5). Against no covariates it is significant after Holm correction at 7, 14, 21 days, not at 28 (p 0.077), the window of the headline. By transition at 28 days: closure to work 86.88% to 22.21%, work to holiday 15.34% to 5.55%, holiday to work 19.18% to 14.59%.
